units.translation: After a long time I boasted that the gods would accomplish these things.
For never did I boast that, dying in this Argive land, I would have a share of a most beloved tomb.
You boast that this deed is mine.
Seeing him who never boasted, worn out by helpless miseries.
For who boasted that this unexpected flight would land?
The correct accent is αὔχη [boast], as κενεόφρονες αὖχαι [empty-minded boasts] in Pindar Nem. 11, 39. Hermann conjectured that the dative αὐχαῖς [boasts] should be supplied in defective fr. 152.
Similar examples are collected in Thes. vol. 1, 2 p. 2593.
It seems now that her neck is about to fall near the razor's edge.
He places the yoke-straps upon their necks.
Having cast the yoke upon the neck of the sea.

Concerning the words quoted by Diogenes Laertius 7, 28 from the Niobe, ἔρχομαι, τί μ᾽ αὐεις [I come, why do you cry to me?], which are not to be referred to a play of Aeschylus, I have spoken on Sophocles fr. 395.
I come, why do you cry to me?
to take away, to snatch away
to take away, to snatch away

which the scholiast explains as ἕως ή νύξ ἐπιγενομένη ἔπαυσεν αὐτοὺς τῆς μάχης [until the night coming on stopped them from battle]. Similar examples are collected in Thes. vol. 1, 2 p. 2603: Thucyd. 4, 134 ἀφελομένης νυκτὸς τὸ ἔργον [night having taken away the work], and Xen. Hell. 1, 2, 16 ἐδίωκε μέχρι σκότος ἀφείλετο [he pursued until darkness took it away].
The man-snatching doom having taken him from the land.
Having taken away the mutual-slaughtering madnesses from the halls.
And hastening to take away some of these cares,
From your last words I will take away a great anxiety.
Until the eye of dark night took it away.
And I was deprived of a great curb of the house.
How shall I say, and by whom deprived, that I have come, a cousinly band of women?
until the night coming on stopped them from battle
night having taken away the work
he pursued until darkness took it away
He leaped a light leap from the ship.
which Triclinius explains as ἤγουν ὥστε ἀφανῆ γενέσθαι καὶ φθαρῆναι [that is, so as to become invisible and be destroyed].
For there is no bulwark of wealth against satiety for a man who has kicked the great altar of Justice into destruction.
that is, so as to become invisible and be destroyed
where, since a long syllable is required, Boeckh conjectured δυσφανῆ [hard to see].
Into the all-receiving and unseen land.
Bull-voiced, they bellow from somewhere out of the unseen, fearful imitators.
A man vanished from the Achaean army.
May I become black smoke, neighboring the clouds of Zeus, and wholly vanished.
Having given orders at once to the infantry army.
What sound, what lightless scent flew to me?
Vomiting the clots of blood which you swallowed down.
And shut out from the inner chamber.
